unite_adi: UPPER SECONDARY-YEAR 10 (AFTER PREP)-LEVEL: B2.2 - THEME 7: LIFE IN NATURE & GLOBAL PROBLEMS

bolumler.ogrenmeKanitlari: PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT: Students will design ''a community action plan'' including sustainable development (eco-friendly buildings, green technology); food security and famine; climate change and its global impact: problems and solutions. They work in pairs. First, they find a global issue such as climate change, food security, or sustainable development. Then they suggest three practical and innovative solutions for either urban or rural environments. They will create a visual representation such as a poster or 3D model of one solution. They will conclude with a short written or oral reflection on how applying the suggested plan can promote balance between human needs and environmental preservation in the classroom. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme. Öğrenme-Öğretme Yaşantıları
bolumler.temelKabuller: This theme includes the concept of ''life in nature and global problems with its components such as sustainable development (eco-friendly buildings, green technology); food security and famine; climate change and its global impact: problems and solutions'' and it is assumed that it could be present in almost all languages, with some exceptions. It is assumed that a student in after prep year 10 of upper secondary school may know what sustainable development (eco-friendly buildings, green technology); food security and famine; climate change and its global impact: problems and solutions mean in their as it is known that almost all people who start to learn a new language bring their pre-existing knowledge (in their own language) with them and transfer it to their new language learning context. However, they may not know how to say these things in a foreign language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. Fortunately, this existing knowledge in their own language can help them recognise, understand, and learn them more easily in a foreign language, in this case English. As they are students in after prep year 10 of upper secondary school, they are expected to know some basic vocabulary about ''life in nature and global problems'' and also some necessary structures in English from the previous themes and/or years. These grammar items and vocabulary are revised during the ''Revision Programme'' at the beginning of the year, and they can be used as a basis for learning the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme, so that the new grammatical elements in the current theme can be learnt easily.
bolumler.onDegerlendirme: It is assumed that these students in after prep year 10 of upper secondary school are ready to learn the concept of ''life in nature and global problems with its components such as sustainable development (ecofriendly buildings, green technology); food security and famine; climate change and its global impact: problems and solutions'' cognitively, affectively, and socially since it is appropriate to their age and language level. Therefore, a contextual poster or a large picture could be provided for the students to remember and practise the items that they are related and previously learnt so that they can discuss about the poster and/ or the picture in pairs and write down what they remember. This session can help them revise all the related vocabulary and grammatical elements that they have already learnt from previous themes or from previous years as a preparatory practice. In this way, their performance can be evaluated in terms of how much they remember and how accurately they use these items to build their competence in the current theme. It can help the teacher decide what to emphasise, revise, and practise in order to facilitate the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme. (Their performance can be evaluated by rubrics, a rating scale, and /or a marking scheme during these practices.).
bolumler.zenginlestirme: Objective: To talk about sustainable development, food security and famine, and climate change and its global impact in English by using the target vocabulary. Activity 1: Role-Play on Global Problems Students take part in a role-play based on real-world scenarios related to sustainable development, food security, and climate change. The teacher assigns roles such as a climate scientist, farmer, etc. S/he provides prompts such as, ''The initiative, which promotes renewable energy, has been implemented in several countries'' to guide their responses. Students engage in a simulated discussion or meeting by addressing topics such as solutions to drought or the benefits of green technology in urban areas (e.g. sustainable, conservation, biodiversity) and relative clauses (e.g. ''The farmer, whose crops were destroyed by drought, is searching for solutions''). After each role play, the teacher gives feedback on correct use of language with target vocabulary and target grammar. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
bolumler.destekleme: Objective: To identify sustainable development, climate change, and its global impact in English by using target vocabulary. Activity 1: Picture Description The teacher shows students some pictures related to sustainable development or climate change (e.g. a solar panel, a drought-stricken area, a wind turbine). S/he provides sentences such as ''This is ______, which ______''. ''The ______, where ______, is ______'' or ''This is a place whose ______'' to guide them. Students write or say sentences by using the pictures and target vocabulary such as ''biodiversity, conservation, or renewable''. For example: ''This is a solar panel, which produces clean energy'' or ''The forest, where many species live, is under threat''. The teacher provides a word bank if students need it. They read the sentences aloud. In the end, the teacher gives constructive feedback on the correct use of language with relative clauses and the target vocabulary. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
